- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/negative.
- If sentiment shows strong negative signals (e.g., -0.3 to -0.8), model frequently underestimates; add 2–4% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in downward corrections; if true price drops below 65, forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–2% per day until stabilization.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values if sentiment is flat or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.10” values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for suppressed market sentiment.
